answers.question: Can a student with an unpaid tuition balance or a pending grade appeal participate in commencement, and will their degree be officially conferred?
answers.actual_answer: A student with an unpaid tuition balance or a pending grade appeal may participate in the commencement ceremony, but their degree will not be officially conferred until all requirements and holds are cleared. A financial hold blocks official conferral and the release of the final transcript, while a pending grade appeal may delay conferral if it affects degree requirements or GPA.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed. A payment plan is available for balances of at least USD 1,000; it requires 40% by the original due date and two equal monthly instalments. Missing an instalment creates a financial hold.

Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.
